issue: The p50, p90, and p95 reference lines are all rendered in the same green dashed style and are packed within a narrow band (~0.80–0.99 s). At print size the three lines are distinguishable mainly by their small stacked labels, not by visual encoding.
evidence: The figure shows p50, p90, and p95 as three closely spaced green dashed vertical lines; only the labels distinguish them. The caption says the percentiles are read off the stream, so the reader must map each label to its line.
acceptance_test: Either give p50/p90/p95 distinct line styles or markers, or add a small inset/legend that maps each percentile to its line without relying on color alone; verify the figure remains readable in grayscale at 100% print size.

issue: The shaded 'SLO-violating' region does not begin at the SLO line. The caption states 'the light band marks the full SLO-violating region (> 2 s); everything right of the SLO line', but the drawn light-pink band starts at approximately 4.4 s, well to the right of the 2 s SLO line, leaving the interval (2 s, ~4.4 s) unshaded.
evidence: In the render, the blue dash-dot SLO line is at x = 2 s and the pink band begins near x = 4.4 s; the darker hatched sub-band covers the ~5 s straggler cluster. The caption's parenthetical '(> 2 s); everything right of the SLO line' describes a band that starts at 2 s. A reader can therefore infer that no request violates the SLO between 2 s and 4.4 s, which is false as a statement about the region (it is empty of data, not empty of violations).
acceptance_test: Either extend the light band to start at the 2 s SLO line, or change the caption to 'the light band marks the straggler cluster region (~4.4-6 s), all of which lies beyond the 2 s SLO line'. Acceptance: the drawn band and the caption describe the same interval.

issue: The annotation box reports 'p99 = 1.33 s' with no qualifier, but 1.33 s is the p99 of the finite N = 10,000 sample, not of the stated workload. The prose on the facing page (printed p. 92) is explicit that 'the population p99 of the stated 99 % log-normal + 1 % straggler mix is 5.0 s' and that the sample p99 'still looks healthy'. The figure alone licenses the wrong inference the section exists to correct.
evidence: Printed p. 92: 'p99 ~ 1.33 s - a knife-edge property of this N = 10,000 sample, not of the distribution ... the population p99 of the stated 99 % log-normal + 1 % straggler mix is 5.0 s'. Figure annotation: 'mean = 0.85 s / p99 = 1.33 s / (p99 still looks fine)'. The caption's 'p50/p90/p95/p99 read off the stream' is not carried into the annotation itself.
acceptance_test: Relabel the annotation to 'sample p99 (N = 10,000) = 1.33 s' and add 'population p99 = 5.0 s' as a second line, so the figure carries the section's actual lesson rather than the trap. Acceptance: a reader who sees only the figure cannot conclude that the workload's p99 is 1.33 s.

issue: The figure plots 'Request latency (s)' and draws an 'SLO 2 s' line, but the prose identifies the same 2 s budget as the canonical p95 TTFT SLO ('Under the canonical p95 TTFT SLO of <= 2 s ...'). TTFT and end-to-end request latency are different quantities (request latency >= TTFT always), so the figure applies a TTFT budget to a request-latency distribution.
evidence: Printed p. 92: 'Under the canonical p95 TTFT SLO of <= 2 s, even this sample's p99 (~ 1.33 s) still looks healthy'; and later on the same page 'We budget TTFT <= 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s) with a p95 <= 2 s.' FIG 6.2's x-axis is 'Request latency (s)' and its caption is 'Request-latency distribution'.
acceptance_test: Decide which quantity the 2 s SLO governs and make the figure and the prose agree: either relabel the axis/line as TTFT, or relabel the line 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget applied to request latency)' and add one clause in the prose noting that request latency is bounded below by TTFT. Acceptance: no page in Ch. 6 uses 'SLO 2 s' for two different metrics.

issue: The p90 (0.94 s) and p95 (0.99 s) reference lines are separated by 0.05 s on a 0-6 s axis, i.e. ~0.8% of the plot width (~2-3 px at 150 dpi). The two green dashed lines are effectively coincident, so the reader cannot verify the p90/p95 values the prose quotes from the figure.
evidence: Prose on printed p. 92 quotes 'p50 ~ 0.80 s, p90 ~ 0.94 s, p95 ~ 0.99 s, and p99 ~ 1.33 s' as read off the plotted histogram. On the rendered page the p90 and p95 lines overlap; only their stacked labels at the top-left distinguish them.
acceptance_test: Add a zoomed inset over the 0.7-1.4 s region, or annotate the percentile values numerically at each line, so p90 and p95 are separately readable at print size.

issue: Two wording defects in the figure's own text: (a) the caption contains a stray unmatched closing parenthesis — 'the light band marks the full SLO-violating region (> 2 s); everything right of the SLO line) and the darker hatched band ...'; (b) the in-plot annotation '1% stragglers (>5 s cross the SLO)' misdescribes the cluster, which is centred at 5 s and spans roughly 4.4-6 s, so only its upper half is '> 5 s'.
evidence: Both strings are legible on the rendered page (printed p. 93). The caption's parenthetical is opened at '(> 2 s)' and closed, then a second ')' appears after 'SLO line' with no matching '('.
acceptance_test: Remove the stray ')' and change the annotation to '1% stragglers (all beyond the 2 s SLO)' or '1% stragglers (~5 s, all beyond the 2 s SLO)'. Acceptance: caption punctuation balances and the annotation's inequality matches the drawn cluster.

issue: The figure draws only three query-head groups followed by an ellipsis, while the label says '× 8 groups'. A reader can momentarily read the drawing as three groups total rather than a schematic excerpt of eight.
evidence: The figure shows three groups of eight query heads, each connected to one K/V head, then '…'. The label below says '8 query heads : 1 K/V head (× 8 groups)'.
acceptance_test: Make the ellipsis and the '× 8 groups' relation visually explicit, e.g. label the three drawn groups as 'group 1 … group 8 (three shown)' or add a bracket/annotation that the drawing is schematic; confirm the 64:8 total is unambiguous.

figure: Figure 7.2 — Hybrid history: two state lifetimes
issue: The top row draws three fixed-size state boxes side by side, which can visually suggest three retained states even though the caption says recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained. The corrective text is present but the layout still carries the wrong first impression.
evidence: The figure shows 'state after t1', 'state after t2', and 'state after t3' as three separate boxes in parallel columns. The caption says 'recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained.'
acceptance_test: Redraw the top row so succession is visually dominant—e.g. a single state box updated in place across t1→t2→t3, or a timeline with explicit 'overwrite' arrows—so a reader cannot infer joint retention from the layout alone.

issue: The figure's own legend states 'Arrows = token input / state flow', but no arrow is drawn from the 'token t1 / t2 / t3' labels into the 'recurrent update' boxes; the only arrows are the horizontal state-flow arrows between update boxes and the vertical arrows from update boxes to state snapshots. Token input is named in the legend but not encoded.
evidence: Rendered page (printed p. 110): 'token t1', 'token t2', 'token t3' sit as bare text labels above the blue 'recurrent update' boxes with no connector; the legend line 'Arrows = token input / state flow' claims both meanings.
acceptance_test: Either add a short downward arrow from each token label into its update box, or amend the legend to 'Arrows = state flow (update to update) and snapshot (update to state)'. Acceptance: every arrow meaning named in the legend is drawn.

issue: The figure's note 'Recurrent updates compute; state and KV boxes store' introduces a compute-vs-storage distinction that the visual language does not carry consistently with the rest of the chapter: KV/state storage is orange in FIG 7.1, red/pink in FIG 7.2, and uncolored gray in FIGS 7.3-7.4.
evidence: FIG 7.1 (printed p. 108): K/V boxes are orange with white 'K/V' text. FIG 7.2 (printed p. 110): state boxes are red-bordered/pink, KV boxes are red-bordered. FIG 7.3 (printed p. 114) and FIG 7.4 (printed p. 116): all boxes/bars are neutral gray. No chapter-level legend maps color to compute vs storage.
acceptance_test: Adopt one chapter-level color convention (e.g. blue = compute, orange = persistent state/KV, gray = format/metadata) and apply it to FIGS 7.1-7.4, or state in the Ch. 7 opening that color is not semantic. Acceptance: the same concept carries the same visual treatment across the chapter's figures.

figure: Figure 7.3 — Quantization choices and execution paths
issue: The execution-path branch is labeled 'Native FP4 math', but the numerical-representation box includes INT4. The figure does not show a native-INT4 path, so a reader may infer that INT4 executes through FP4 math or that the branch applies to all listed formats.
evidence: Top-right box: 'INT4 + scheme / MXFP4 / NVFP4'. Bottom-left branch: 'Native FP4 math / Compatible low-bit operand arithmetic'. The caption says only supported combinations can load and execute.
acceptance_test: Either relabel the branch to cover the actual native path(s) (e.g. 'Native low-bit math (format-dependent)') or add a note that native FP4 math applies only to FP4 formats and INT4 follows a different dispatch path; verify the diagram does not imply a universal execution path.

issue: The outer container box is titled 'Packed tensors: values + scales (+ zero points, if used)', yet the note inside the same box reads 'Container wraps tensors + metadata: e.g., GGUF / safetensors'. The box therefore conflates the checkpoint file format (the container) with the packed tensor payload (its content), and the inner box ('Layout, padding and alignment are implementation-specific') has no title of its own. The reader cannot tell which box is the file and which is the payload.
evidence: Rendered structure: large rounded rectangle whose bold heading is 'Packed tensors: values + scales (+ zero points, if used)', containing a smaller titled box 'Layout, padding and alignment are implementation-specific' and the note 'Container wraps tensors + metadata: e.g., GGUF / safetensors'. The caption refers to 'packed tensors and checkpoint container' as two distinct things, which the drawing does not show.
acceptance_test: Retitle the outer box 'Checkpoint container (e.g., GGUF / safetensors)' and move 'Packed tensors: values + scales (+ zero points, if used)' to the inner box heading. Acceptance: the drawing shows two distinct, correctly named levels matching the caption's vocabulary.

issue: The three bottom boxes ('Native FP4 math', 'Fused dequant', 'Reconstruct') are mutually exclusive execution paths, but the connector from 'Runtime tensors in the kernel-required layout' fans into them without any 'one of' marker, so the diagram can be read as a sequential pipeline.
evidence: The connector is a single horizontal line with three downward arrows; the only disambiguation is the note below the row ('Only supported combinations can load and execute.'). The caption's 'Unsupported combinations may be rejected' reinforces the alternatives reading but is not in the drawing.
acceptance_test: Add an 'exactly one of' label or a brace on the fan-out, so the alternatives reading is carried by the diagram rather than only by the caption.

issue: The subtitle asserts 'Payload and local-scale bar widths are proportional to bytes', but the two 1-byte NVFP4 scale segments are drawn at roughly half the width of the 1-byte MXFP4 scale segment, so within-bar proportionality does not hold.
evidence: In the render, the MXFP4 row's single dark segment (1 B scale) is about twice the width of each of the NVFP4 row's two dark segments (2 B scales total). The payload segments are consistent (~21 px/B in both rows), so the discrepancy is confined to the scale segments, which are drawn at a minimum visible width rather than proportionally.
acceptance_test: Measure the source drawing: each 1-byte scale segment should be 1/16 of the 16-byte payload segment. If it is not, either redraw proportionally (with a minimum-width floor stated in the subtitle) or amend the subtitle to 'payload widths are proportional to bytes; scale segments are drawn at a minimum legible width'.

figure: FIGURE 7.5 (KV cache size vs context, by attention geometry)
issue: The caption's 'Scope:' sentence is internally incoherent and contradicts the figure's own legend and annotations. As rendered it reads (fragments): 'Scope: FP16 is 2.62 MB/token, FP8 is half that, ~1.31 GB (vs the ~436 GB budget) at 128K for the FP16 full-MHA footprint is ~535 GB (vs the ~436 GB budget); the GQA FP8 footprint, ~24.9 GB at 9.5K (total tokens with KV residency) — then ~16 GB (vs the ~436 GB budget).' Each of the four numeric claims fails against the figure's own encoding.
evidence: Recomputation from the legend values (2.62 MB/tok full-MHA FP16; 0.33 MB/tok GQA FP8): (a) 'FP8 is half that, ~1.31 GB' — the per-token FP8 value is ~1.31 MB/token (also stated in the figure's own note above the legend: '~1.31 MB/token'); 'GB' is a 1000x unit error. (b) 'the GQA FP8 footprint, ~24.9 GB at 9.5K' — 9,500 x 0.33 MB = 3.1 GB, which is exactly what the figure's own annotation says ('9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)'); 24.9 GB is the full-MHA FP16 value (9,500 x 2.62 MB = 24.9 GB), i.e. the caption attributes the full-MHA number to the GQA curve. (c) 'at 128K ... ~535 GB' — 128,000 x 2.62 MB = 335 GB; the drawn full-MHA FP16 marker at x=128 sits BELOW the 436 GB budget line, consistent with 335 GB and inconsistent with 535 GB. (d) 'then ~16 GB' — GQA FP8 at 128K = 128,000 x 0.33 MB = 42 GB; 16 GB corresponds to no quantity in the figure. The sentence also contains three parenthetical '(vs the ~436 GB budget)' insertions and a run-on with no grammatical subject, indicating an editing failure rather than a single typo.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the 'Scope:' sentence so that every number is (i) recomputed from the legend's per-token values, (ii) consistent with the two in-plot annotations ('9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)', '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)'), and (iii) consistent with the drawn marker positions at x=128. Specifically: FP8 = ~1.31 MB/token; full-MHA FP16 at 9.5K = 24.9 GB and at 128K = ~335 GB (below the 436 GB budget); GQA FP8 at 9.5K = 3.1 GB and at 128K = ~42 GB. Then re-render and confirm the caption contains no number that is not derivable from the legend.

issue: The caption states 'GQA with a 64:1 query:to-KV head ratio is 8x lower'. A 64:1 query-to-KV ratio is MQA and would reduce KV by 64x, not 8x. The book's own geometry (FIG 7.1, printed p. 108: '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)' = 64 query heads, 8 KV heads) is 64:8, which is what produces the 8x saving shown in the figure and the '8x saving (Ch. 7)' annotation.
evidence: FIG 7.1 annotation: '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)'. FIG 7.5 legend: full-MHA FP16 ~2.62 MB/tok vs GQA FP16 ~0.66 MB/tok (4x) and GQA FP8 ~0.33 MB/tok (8x). The 8x figure is consistent with 64:8, not 64:1. The caption as rendered therefore states a head ratio that contradicts both the figure it captions and the preceding figure in the same chapter.
acceptance_test: Confirm the ratio string in the source. If it reads '64:1', change to '64:8' (or '8:1 per group'); if it reads '64:8', no change. In either case, add a one-clause cross-reference to FIG 7.1 so the 8x factor is traceable to the head geometry rather than asserted.

issue: The caption contains a duplicated clause and a lowercase sentence start, both visible in the rendered page: 'The full-MHA FP16 curve is the conservative upper-bound baseline; GQA with a 64:1 query:to-KV head ratio is 8x smaller; full-MHA does the conservative upper-bound baseline.' and 'GQA, FP8/8-bit). parameter count does not determine KV size'.
evidence: The clause 'full-MHA does the conservative upper-bound baseline' restates the first clause of the same sentence. The sentence beginning 'parameter count does not determine KV size' follows a full stop and a closing parenthesis but begins with a lowercase 'p'. Both are visible on the rendered page (printed p. 123, caption lines 2 and 4-5).
acceptance_test: Delete the duplicated clause and capitalize 'Parameter'. Re-render and confirm the caption reads as a sequence of complete, non-redundant sentences.

issue: The two horizontal reference lines in the legend — '8xH100 (raw, 640 GB)' and 'KV budget ~436 GB' — are separated by only 0.17 decades on a 4-decade logarithmic y-axis (log10(640)=2.81, log10(436)=2.64). At print size they are effectively coincident, and neither line is labelled in place, so a reader cannot tell which dashed line is which or where the full-MHA FP16 curve crosses the budget.
evidence: Plot y-axis spans 0.1 to 1000 GB (4 decades). The two reference values differ by 640/436 = 1.47x, i.e. 0.17 decades = ~4% of the axis height. In the 150 dpi render the two dashed lines are within a few pixels of each other; the legend is the only disambiguator, and the legend entries are themselves distinguished only by dash colour (grey vs blue), which is a colour-only distinction that degrades in grayscale.
acceptance_test: At 100% print size, confirm the two reference lines are individually traceable. If not: label each line in place (e.g. '8xH100 = 640 GB' at the right end of the line, 'KV budget ~436 GB' likewise), and/or replace the 640 GB line with a single annotated line, and/or add an explicit marker where the full-MHA FP16 curve crosses the 436 GB budget (~166K tokens). Ensure the two lines differ by more than dash pattern alone.
